item.title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01331-8

Ballester and Tran-Nguyen advocate for transparency in data, code and experimental procedures in the evaluation of protein–ligand predictions. They discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and bias, enabling fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across different scoring methods.
item.dc:title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction

item.title: Efficient equivariant framework for universal charge density prediction
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01326-5

Li et al. introduce EdenGNN-Uni, a universal charge density model for the periodic table that is over an order of magnitude faster than some existing methods, facilitating efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations of materials.
